title: Four Players of Indian Heritage Will Take the Field at the FIFA World Cup. None of Them Play for India.
excerpt: From Punjab to Auckland, Kerala to Doha, and Tamil Nadu to Melbourne — the diaspora will be represented at football's grandest stage even as the Blue Tigers watch from home.
body:
The FIFA World Cup 2026 begins on June 11 across the United States, Canada and Mexico. India, as expected, will not be there. The Blue Tigers crashed out in the second round of qualifying, continuing a drought that stretches back to 1950 — the only time India has ever qualified.

But this time, Indian football fans have a reason to watch that goes beyond neutral fandom. At least four players of Indian heritage will feature in the tournament, representing four different nations across four different continents. It is a quiet testament to the reach of the diaspora — and a bittersweet reminder of where Indian football itself stands.

## Sarpreet Singh — New Zealand

The most prominent name on this list is Sarpreet Singh, the 27-year-old attacking midfielder whose parents emigrated from Jalandhar, Punjab, to Auckland. Singh came through the Wellington Phoenix academy in New Zealand's A-League before earning a move to Bayern Munich in 2019 — becoming the first player of Indian descent to sign for the German giants.

After loan spells at Nürnberg and Regensburg in the 2. Bundesliga, Singh returned to New Zealand football and has rebuilt his career after a difficult run of injuries. He now has 26 caps for the All Whites and was confirmed in their final roster for the World Cup.

"When the coach told me I was selected, it was such a special and proud moment," Singh told Livemint in an exclusive interview from Miami, where the team is based. "The last few months have been tough with injuries. It was a nice reward at the end of hard work."

When New Zealand face Iran in their Group G opener on June 16 in California, Singh will become the first Indian-origin footballer at a World Cup since France's Vikash Dhorasoo in 2006. New Zealand are also drawn alongside Belgium and Egypt.

## Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid — Qatar

The youngest player on this list is just 19. Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid was born in Doha to parents from Kannur, Kerala, and came through Qatar's elite Aspire Academy before signing with Al Duhail in the Qatar Stars League — making him the first player of Indian origin to feature in Qatar's top flight.

Jamshid's selection in Qatar's final 26-man squad prompted a wave of pride back in Kerala, India's most football-obsessed state. Congress MP Shashi Tharoor posted on social media: "Kerala has always loved football with an ardour bordering on devotion, yet for all our passion we had never sent one of our own to the sport's grandest stage — until now."

Qatar are in Group B alongside Canada, Switzerland and Bosnia and Herzegovina. If Jamshid takes the field, he will be the first Malayali to play at a FIFA World Cup.

## Nishan Velupillay — Australia

Melbourne Victory winger Nishan Velupillay brings Tamil heritage to the Socceroos' World Cup squad. The 25-year-old was born in Melbourne to a Malaysian father of Tamil descent and an Anglo-Indian mother. He came through the Victory academy and has made 128 A-League appearances, earning his first cap for Australia in a World Cup qualifier against China.

Velupillay's pace and direct attacking play have made him a fan favourite in Melbourne, and his six caps suggest he is more than a tokenistic selection. Australia are in Group D with the United States, Türkiye and Paraguay — a tough draw, but one where the Socceroos will fancy their chances of advancing.

For NRIs in the United States, the Australia-USA group game in Houston on June 18 could be a particularly compelling affair.

## Samuel Moutoussamy — DR Congo

The least obvious Indian connection belongs to Samuel Moutoussamy, the 29-year-old defensive midfielder who represents the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Born in Paris to an Indo-Guadeloupean father with Tamil heritage and a Congolese mother, Moutoussamy opted to represent the Leopards and has earned 57 caps since 2019.

After 144 appearances for Nantes in Ligue 1, he moved through the Netherlands and Turkey before settling at Greek side Atromitos. He is one of the most experienced members of a Congolese squad that faces Portugal, Colombia and Uzbekistan in Group K.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

The presence of these four players — from Punjab, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and the French-Indian diaspora — speaks to a broader truth about Indian football. The talent exists, scattered across the world, shaped by different systems, different leagues, different pathways. What India lacks is not potential but infrastructure.

For the 18 million NRIs watching from abroad, and the hundreds of millions in India who will tune in on Zee5 and UNITE8 Sports after the last-minute broadcast deal was signed, these four players offer a personal stake in a tournament that has historically felt like someone else's party.

The World Cup runs from June 11 to July 19 across 16 venues in the United States, Canada and Mexico. For the first time, 48 teams will compete. India will not be among them. But Indians will be on the pitch.
author: Diaspora Desk
